A large corporation takes over OutTV, completely revamping Jack's talk show and giving him a conservative co-host, Britney Spears.
Jack loses his hosting job and vows never to return to acting; Will has a showdown with his father.
At his father's funeral, Will grapples with their last encounter; Grace begins to doubt her potential to be a good mother.
Will and Grace attend childbirth classes; Karen seeks comfort from very busy Jack.
Vince's plans to move into a brownstone with Will do not include Grace; Jack's show premieres.
Will and Grace make a decision about their future together; Jack continues his never-ending search for love; Karen tries to find happiness in Stan's absence.
Will and Grace both falter when their political beliefs are put to the test; Jack and Karen help Will and Grace hide their secret shame from each other, but the truth finally comes out.
Will and Jack try to date younger guys but find it challenging; Grace and Karen experience a crisis that reveals Grace's true feelings about Karen.
Grace finds that the emergency contact called by her doctor's office is ex-husband Leo, not Will; Jack takes on a new job; Karen befriends a 12-year-old girl in the Bronx.
Jack is stunned to learn that his estranged son has a son of his own; Grace and Karen behave badly with the hot new guy at work.
Grace gets a job decorating a string of boutique hotels for an obnoxious hotel mogul; Will is surprised at his reaction to becoming senior partner; Jack owns half of a winning lottery ticket.
Karen has trouble dealing with a personal tragedy; Will, Grace, and Jack try to intervene; Will and Grace's new business relationship begins to show signs of stress.
Will, Grace, Karen and Jack wish they could have experienced Christmas in old New York, but realize the past was not quite as romantic or open to diversity as they pictured it.
Will and Grace try to convince themselves they are okay with dating the same man; Jack and Karen get an annoying commercial jingle stuck in their heads and must seek medical attention.
Will and Grace's old friend Larry decides he's in love with Will; Jack's first day as a Lyft driver doesn't go as planned; Karen tries to help Jack but ends up needing help rather than giving it.
Grace tries to prevent Will from making a scene at his ex-boyfriend's wedding; Jack's wedding hook-up comes with strings attached.
Jack's intimacy issues are challenged by a closeted boyfriend; Will and Grace sell their new line of bedding on live television.

Grace is horrified to realize that she's dated three men from the same family; Will and Karen get on each other's nerves at the office until they bond over watching -- and producing -- their own little telenovela.
A baby shower makes Grace and Will question their life choices; Karen and Jack find a way to combine child labor with musical theater.
Against Jack's advice, Will rekindles a relationship with his first love; Grace reluctantly fights for Karen's civil rights when a bakery refuses to make a cake she wants.
Grace brings Will for support when she goes home to celebrate her deceased mother's birthday; Jack's faith in love is crushed after a breakup; a secret in Karen's marriage is uncovered.
Grace's father and Will's mother end up making a surprising and upsetting connection; Jack rebounds from his breakup with a new love; Karen must decide between her husband and her lover.

Grace's accidental run-in with a curmudgeon she follows on Twitter smacks of romance; Jack makes a terrible impression on Estefan's family after a numbing cream incident; Will helps Karen protect her most prized possession.

After Will and Grace's parents get married, big changes are afoot for the gang: Will gets a teaching job and a beard, Grace decides to run for office, Jack prepares to settle down with Estefan and Karen goes missing.
Jack fears for his grandson's safety at a Texas talent show; Grace and Noah try to have sex.
Now a certified psychic, Jack channels Rosario to help Karen open her heart to love again; Grace learns love means having to say she's sorry.

While on a road trip with her father, Grace reveals a past secret, changing their relationship forever; legendary drag queen Miss Coco Peru emcees a lip sync monologue throw down to determine who will be Jack's best man, Will or Karen.

When Will discovers Noah has a child, he promises to keep the secret from Grace; Karen and Jack's relationship is tested when she fires him from the play she's producing and replaces him with Jon Cryer.

Zack's (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) advice line backfires and gets him into trouble with everyone. With Mario Lopez.

Zack makes a surprising discovery about his Native American heritage; Lisa learns her family tree includes a Black American hero of the Underground Railroad; Jessie grapples with guilt over her slave-trading ancestry.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) asks Kelly (Tiffani-Amber Thiessen) to go steady and then falls in love with the school nurse.
Mr. Belding's brother Rod (guest star Edward Blatchford) scores points with the class as a substitute history teacher. With Dennis Haskins and Mark-Paul Gosselaar.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) plots to reunite Slater (Mario Lopez), Mr. Belding (Dennis Haskins) and himself with their feuding sweethearts.
Some underhanded shenanigans are employed to win a glee club competition.
A costume ball sets the stage for Zack and Kelly (Mark-Paul Gosselaar, Tiffani-Amber Thiessen) to examine their relationship.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) has a hard time dealing with the fact that Kelly (Tiffani-Amber Thiessen) has a new boyfriend.
A minor accident sends Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) to the hospital, where he nervously faces the prospect of surgery.
Panic hits when Screech (Dustin Diamond) finds out he has to play a Russian exchange student in the chess finals. With Dennis Haskins.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) tries to impress a college girl by lying about his age.
The students adopt a new mascot when a stray ball injures a duck in the pond behind the football field.
Jessie's stepbrother Eric arrives from New York and blackmails her, Zack and Slater (Elizabeth Berkley, Mark-Paul Gosselaar, Mario Lopez).
Eric tries to blackmail Slater (Mario Lopez) and learns a disturbing truth about his date with Lisa (Lark Voorhies).
The student council decides to hold a dance-date auction to raise money for new cheerleading uniforms.

When a girl isn't allowed to try out for the wrestling team, the students band together and protest the decision.

Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) is in love with Stacy (Leah Remini) but fears she is only interested in her college boyfriend.
Stacy (Leah Remini), in charge of the club for the day, learns her father booked two parties for the same night. With Mario Lopez.
The entire gang goes to the mall to obtain U2 tickets and ends up camping out overnight. With Mark-Paul Gosselaar and Mario Lopez.
Stacy (Leah Remini) moves out after her father forbids her to see Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar).
Jessie's father invites everyone to his Palm Springs resort to attend his wedding. With Elizabeth Berkley and Mario Lopez.
Casey Kasem (guest starring as himself) chronicles the rise of the rock group Zack Attack. With Mark-Paul Gosselaar.
The students are shocked during the Christmas season to discover the new girl working in Mr. Moody's store is homeless.
Zack's family invites Laura and her father home for Christmas.

Zack's plan to encourage the teachers to strike backfires on the students when the Academic Bowl is canceled.
The gang scrambles for dates as the senior prom approaches. With Mark-Paul Gosselaar and Mario Lopez.
A look into the future finds Belding with six students who are very similar to the gang from the class of 1993.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) is desperate enough to try ballet class when he learns he needs one more credit to graduate.
Zack's partner for a school project is the new girl at Bayside, a tough biker who is not at all impressed with him.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) becomes overprotective of the physically challenged girl he is counseling on the teen line.
Zack and Slater (Mark-Paul Gosselaar, Mario Lopez) bet to see who can kiss Tori (Leanna Creel) first.

On location for the production of the "Sweeney" movie, guest Ryan Reynolds.
Mobility scooters that can handle the British countryside, guest Michael Fassbender.
A tribute to Swedish carmaker Saab; Matt Smith in the reasonably priced car.

The guys attempt to drive the length of Vietnam in just eight days.
The guys race from London to Edinburgh, traveling by locomotive, motorbike and a Jaguar XK120.
Finding the perfect car for a seventeen-year-old; a race between a McLaren F1 and a Bugatti Veyron.
Deadly toys in the British Army's arsenal; racing the Royal Mail across the British Isles.
Jeremy Clarkson, Richard Hammond and James May find themselves entered in a terrifying French ice race; Sienna Miller is the "Star in a Reasonably Priced Car."
Classic cars are put to the test against modern machines; Brian Johnson.

Jim is sent to Moose Creek, Canada, to identify the corpse of an outlaw only he has seen, but the man was killed with a shotgun blast to the face, which makes him hard to identify; a woman claims the body is her brother's body.
The son of a dead man accused of a stage coach robbery finds an empty strongbox in the attic and hopes that Jim Hardie can help him uncover the real thieves.
Hardie gives a job to the son of a former employee who was fired.
Hardie tries to prevent a lynching when a town's hard cases accuse a Basque sheepherder of the abduction of a young girl.
Jim goes undercover as a trainee for Wells Fargo, to try and find out who is supplying renegade Indians with the guns they are using on their murderous raids.
Hardie isn't pleased when a man and beautiful woman insist on becoming passengers on the stagecoach he will use.
Jim Hardie is ordered to infiltrate Sam Bass' gang so that he can learn where they hole up between raids.
A strong-willed woman takes Flint prisoner when he asks permission to cross her land.
Flint meets a mother who wants him to marry one of her daughters.
Adams meets a boy who is running away from an abusive father.
An exiled Italian duke charms both the single and the married women.
On Christmas Eve, a young boy wanders off to find Santa Claus.
Flint goes in search of a young woman who was taken by Indians as a child.
Maj. Adams searches for the parties responsible for leaving a woman near death.
Friends locked in a senseless feud.
A beautiful woman teaches her son to hold the weak and helpless in contempt.
Flint brings a young boy to San Francisco to live with his uncle.
A small band of travelers makes its way through the desert for a rendezvous with the wagon train.
The wagon train runs low on water and the passengers look for a new watering place.
Jess gets a call for help from his old partner, Dixie Howard, who once saved Jess' life, but the man Jess once knew has changed.
With an increase of Sioux attacks on the stage, Slim suggests repairing an old road as an alternate route.
Slim Sherman represents the stage line in a contract with an outlaw's widow, who is also a secret investigator.

Slim and Jess come to the aid of a family of entertainers whose wagon breaks down as they travel East; unbeknownst to all, the family is being followed by a group of men who think the family is transporting opium.
Slim and Jess are in dire need of a housekeeper, so the judge will allow them to keep Mike on the ranch.
Jim Hardie joins a group of passengers aboard a stagecoach that includes a woman and her son, a reporter and an outlaw.
When Jesse James and his gang are suspected of robbing a bank in Missouri, Jim Hardie goes undercover to try to find the outlaw.
Hardie is called to investigate when a Wells Fargo agent dies and a large sum of money is determined to be missing from the man's office.
Outlaw Belle Starr and her gang rob a train on which Jim Hardie is a passenger, and he tries to lure her from hiding by tempting her with a prominent racehorse.

A rookie outlaw holds up the stage carrying cash that Jim is waiting for, prompting Jim to go off looking for the thief, but he finds he needs the criminal's help when the two must evade an Indian attack.
Jim joins a father who's searching for his missing son in the Superstition Mountains -- an area held sacred by the Apaches.
As the only witness to a robbery, Hardie is targeted by the robber's partner.
Jim goes on the hunt for a band of robbers that is targeting Pony Express riders.
Jim Hardie is sent to negotiate a right of way for their stagecoaches through Sam Brundage's property.
Hardie investigates a stagecoach holdup where white men disguised as Indians kill the driver and the guard and leave a lady for dead.
At the Wells Fargo auction, a man and a woman bid vigorously on a destroyed suitcase.
Hardie is sent in when a stagecoach is robbed near the Arizona-New Mexico border, and he learns that the only thing taken was a scrappy dog whose collar may be evidence to prove a murder.
Jim Hardie and his Wells Fargo agents set a trap for the notorious Stillwell gang, but the outlaws manage to outwit the detectives and escape with five thousand dollars.
Jim Hardie tries to clear a colleague of a murder charge after the man is found standing over a dead man, holding a smoking gun.
The Wells Fargo team is tasked with protecting a shipment of jade in San Francisco.
Hardie rides with a bigoted general on a mission to quell a Sioux uprising.
A man becomes jealous of the attention his wife showers on their infant son.
Fugitive risks capture to see a friend.
A convict joins the wagon train in search of her long-lost son.
Portlass abducts McCullough in order to find Montezuma's treasure.
A struggling actor invites a fellow actor to his apartment to rehearse a role for which they are competing.
A policeman working the night shift encounters an old man with amnesia (Claude Rains) and a lost boy (Bill Mumy).
Taking advantage of his girlfriend's job at a psychiatrist's office, a small-time crook cooks up a lucrative money-making scheme.
A man's (Andrew Prine) confidence in a faith healer (Sidney Blackmer) leads to an interesting situation for both of them. With Maggie Pierce and Robert Armstrong.
In his run from the law, an escaped convict kidnaps a young woman, unaware of her relationship to his latest victim.
Following a train accident, a man plans to cheat an insurance company out of a large amount of money.
Following the close of a murder trial, an attorney continues to seek the truth for his own personal satisfaction.
On the verge of losing his job, an advertising executive is desperate to come up with a successful ad campaign.
A gang of teen thieves hits one house too many when they target a mob gangster's (Philip Reed) home. With Tom Gilleran and Rafael Campos.
A retired man plans to run away with his mistress and stolen company funds, but his wife has something else in mind.
A man and his lover (Mark Miller, Patricia Breslin) plot to eliminate his wife (Vivienne Segal) so they can be together.
An undertaker (John Fielder) attempts to collect from a penny-pinching killer (Ed Gardner).
A seedy character (Frankie Darro) discovers an amazing formula and decides to use it to make some quick cash. With Robert Keith and Karl Lukas.

A jewelry shop owner sells a rare black pearl to a client, who later returns looking for another one to make a matched pair.

A shoplifter (Coleen Gray) is blackmailed into helping the store manager (Richard Long) in a crime of his own.
A meek clerk (Dick York) plots with his associates to rob their investment firm. With Wendell Holmes.
A wanted man (Jack Carson) disappears while visiting a little-known tourist attraction in Italy. With Christopher Dark.
A recently-divorced man (Robert Webber) makes a deal with a friend (Jeremy Slate) to avoid having to pay alimony.
A man (Wayne Rogers) decides to demonstrate to his new-found girlfriend (Anne Helm) how he gets his kicks. With Brian Hutton.
A housekeeper make arrangements to keep her lover all to herself when he expresses interest in another woman.
A woman (Linda Purl) is attacked in her home and her husband (David Clennon) takes the law into his own hands.
Two retired insurance salesmen (Robert H. Harris, John Qualen) expect murder when the temperature reaches 92 degrees.
A young man (John Forsythe) returns home after an absence of four years to investigate his father's death.
A woman (Ellen Corby) tries to prevent a shootout between two gunslingers (Darren McGavin, Gene Barry).
A determined detective (Robert Emhardt) uncovers a man's scheme to have his "missing" wife declared legally dead.
A woman (Patricia Hitchcock) visiting Paris returns to her hotel room to find her ailing mother missing.
A gangster (Gene Barry) plans to punish the woman (Nancy Gates) he feels is responsible for his brother's death.
A businessman, injured in a car crash and believed by everyone to be dead, fights to signal he is alive.
A man (Everett Sloane) suspects his cook (Beulah Bondi) of being an arsenic-poisoning murderer. With Janet Ward.
A down-on-his-luck man responds to a newspaper ad from a man seeking a companion for a cross-country trip.
A man (Tom Ewell) believes an exact double is gradually taking over his life.
A woman (Judith Evelyn) is suspected of murdering her husband, who has been having an affair with another woman. With Joe Mantell and Kathleen McGuire.
A larcenous store Santa (Barry Fitzgerald) helps change the ways of a potential delinquent (Bobby Clark).
A man (Darren McGavin) tries to trick an elderly woman (Patricia Collinge) out of a family heirloom.
A man (John Qualen) is surprised to learn that the boss he thought he had murdered is still alive. With Philip Reed.
A gunman (George Mathews), intent on murdering his girlfriend, purchases an alibi.
An escaped convict (John Cassavetes) takes refuge in a farmhouse occupied by a young housewife (Marisa Pavan).
A year after the murders, a newspaper reporter (Joan Lorring) attempts to interview Lizzie Borden (Carmen Mathews) and her sister about the killings.
A bum (Robert Newton) witnesses a murder and decide to take advantage of the situation. With Philip Reed.
A police detective (Charles Bronson) investigating a murder focuses on a strange ventriloquist (Claude Rains).
A female reporter (Claire Trevor) encounters problem trying to leave Eastern Europe after meeting a soccer star.
A man (Mark Damon) arrives at a monastery bent on revenge and is convinced by a kind priest (Everett Sloane) to mend his heart.
An English man (John Williams) murders his wife and moves to California, thinking he has committed the perfect crime.
Two greedy brothers plan to murder their elderly aunt (Mildred Natwick) in an attempt to inherit her money.
A desperate couple (Charles Bronson, Norma Crane) plans to rob an eccentric old woman (Estelle Winwood).
An angel (Alan Napier) allows a murdered mystery writer (John Williams) to return to Earth to uncover his killer.
An unemployed man (John Qualen) needing money is hired by an unknown employer (Lorne Greene) to commit murder.
